"=== Sub-Agent Verification Report ===
Target: org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)

If your static analysis strongly suggests the bug is here, YOU MAY re-nominate this method using DIFFERENT 'target_lines' or 'verification_goal'."

`ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` is the buggy method.

Diagnosis:
- The failing test calls `ArrayUtils.add((String[]) null, (String) null)`.
- In `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)`:
  - if `array != null`, it uses `array.getClass()`
  - else if `element != null`, it uses `element.getClass()`
  - else it falls back to `Object.class`
- So when both arguments are `null`, it chooses `Object.class` and calls `copyArrayGrow1(null, Object.class)`.
- `copyArrayGrow1(...)` then returns a new `Object[1]`.
- Back in `add`, that `Object[]` is unchecked-cast to `T[]` and returned.
- At the test call site, the result is being used as `String[]`, so the runtime tries to treat the returned `Object[]` as `String[]`, producing:
  - `ClassCastException: [Ljava.lang.Object; cannot be cast to [Ljava.lang.String;`

Why this is a bug:
- The method cannot infer a valid component type when both `array` and `element` are `null`.
- The expected behavior from the test is to throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
- Instead, it silently creates an `Object[]`, which is type-unsafe and leads to the wrong exception later.

Supporting static evidence:
- `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` lines 3292–3295 choose `Object.class` when both are null.
- `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` line 3298 unchecked-casts the returned array to `T[]`.
- `ArrayUtils.copyArrayGrow1(Object, Class<?>)` line 3535 creates `Array.newInstance(newArrayComponentType, 1)`, i.e. `new Object[1]` in this case.

So the root cause is:
- `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` mishandles the `(null, null)` case and should throw `IllegalArgumentException` instead of manufacturing an `Object[]`.
